output:
Clean through the slopwatch gate. ~250 words:

---

# Dark mode is here

Dark mode ships today in Margin 2.4, on iOS, Android, and the web app.

It took us longer than it should have. The first build was an inverted stylesheet, and it looked like one: grey text floating on grey, every highlight color screaming. We threw it out in March and started again from the paper up.

What we landed on is a background at `#16161a` rather than pure black, because true black on OLED makes text edges shimmer when you scroll. Body text sits at 87% white. Highlights, tags, and backlink chips were all re-tuned to stay readable at that contrast. The yellow highlight went through eleven revisions before it stopped looking radioactive.

Code blocks get their own treatment. Syntax colors come from a modified Nord palette, and inline code no longer vanishes into the surrounding paragraph.

Turn it on in Settings, then Appearance. Three options: Light, Dark, and System, which follows your OS and flips at sunset if your phone does. There is a separate switch for true black, if you want the OLED battery savings and can live with the shimmer.

One thing we skipped: images and PDF attachments stay as they are. Dimming a screenshot to match the theme sounded clever in a design review and looked broken on a real note.

If something in your notes renders wrong, whether a pasted table, an old custom theme, or an embed, mail us at support@margin.app. Screenshots help.
